_comment: Declared-limitation registry (ADR-035, gate.py): every check that may record a declared limitation, with the measurement that shows it and the harness versions it was measured on. A declaration is re-measured on every run: one that stops reproducing fails as escalated, one that reproduces on a version not listed here passes and the run publishes this file with the version added (expected.next.json). `*` is refused.

adaptive.reason: Codex has no documented way to disable explicit `$skill` invocation; `allow_implicit_invocation: false` leaves it invocable by the person
adaptive.measurement: the model-only Skill is listed in the person's skill catalog

adaptive.reason: Codex has no documented way to disable explicit `$skill` invocation
adaptive.measurement: typing `$flow:analyze` put the model-only Skill's body in the model request

adaptive.reason: OpenCode V2 defines no field that hides a Skill from the person (`slash` was removed)
adaptive.measurement: the model-only Skill is listed in the `/skills` browser

adaptive.reason: OpenCode V2 expands any Skill a person mentions (`@id`)
adaptive.measurement: mentioning `@flow:analyze` put the model-only Skill's body in the model request

adaptive.reason: Antigravity drops an agent that carries `model`, so UZE leaves the field out and the agent runs on the session's model
adaptive.measurement: the dispatched agent's request names the session's model, not the block's

adaptive.reason: Claude Code's native build searches through Bash (`grep` is its bundled ugrep) and offers `Grep` to the main model only on opt-in (`--allowedTools`/`--tools`) or to a subagent whose tools name it without Bash
adaptive.measurement: the main session's request declares no `Grep`

adaptive.reason: Claude Code's native build searches through Bash (`grep` is its bundled ugrep) and offers `Grep` to the main model only on opt-in (`--allowedTools`/`--tools`) or to a subagent whose tools name it without Bash
adaptive.measurement: the session did not offer `Grep`, so no search reached the `search.files` group

adaptive.reason: Codex 0.160 writes and edits files through `apply_patch`, which reaches a hook with the whole patch in `command` and no path field, so the alias cannot carry the `path` it promises; UZE leaves it unbound
adaptive.measurement: the census saw the call reach hooks as `apply_patch` with `{"command"}` alone, and no group ran with the alias

adaptive.reason: Codex 0.160 writes and edits files through `apply_patch`, which reaches a hook with the whole patch in `command` and no path field, so the alias cannot carry the `path` it promises; UZE leaves it unbound
adaptive.measurement: the census saw the call reach hooks as `apply_patch` with `{"command"}` alone, and no group ran with the alias

adaptive.reason: Claude Code renders every PreToolUse denial as `PreToolUse:<tool> hook error: <reason>`, the documented `permissionDecision: deny` JSON on exit 0 included; a hand-written hook with no UZE in it shows the same (experiments/claude/deny-render)
adaptive.measurement: the turn that a delivered guard denied shows `hook error` beside the denial's reason

adaptive.reason: Claude Code hands a command the `Monitor` tool starts to the hooks that match `Bash`, which "can block or ask, but not approve or rewrite those commands" (2.1.314, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md); a `shell` deny holds there (`hooks-deny-carrier-blocked`), a transform does not
adaptive.measurement: the transform group ran on the `Monitor` command as `shell`, and the command ran as the model asked (`from-carrier`), not rewritten

adaptive.reason: OpenCode V2's permission prompt renders the call and never the request's message, so the handler's reason is not shown when it asks (tui/src/routes/session/permission.tsx)
adaptive.measurement: the prompt OpenCode showed for the asked call did not carry the handler's reason

adaptive.reason: Codex hook entries have no setting that blocks a call when the hook command cannot start; a handler that never runs lets the call through
adaptive.measurement: with the delivered wrapper deleted, the denied shell call ran

adaptive.reason: Antigravity gates `/compact` behind the server-side experiment flag `enable-compact-slash-command`, which the offline Lab's recorded flag set does not carry, so a session cannot be compacted on demand here
adaptive.measurement: typing `/compact` answers `Unknown command: /compact` and the next turn's request still carries the first turn's prompt

adaptive.reason: Antigravity documents a PostToolUse hook's output as an empty object and reads no decision there. Up to 1.4.2 an output it could not read replaced the tool's result with an error carrying the hook's text, which is how the reason reached the conversation; 1.4.3 logs it and keeps the result (google-antigravity/antigravity-cli#1282). The declaration fails the day a post-tool denial's reason reaches the model.
adaptive.measurement: the post-tool guard ran on the marked command, and its reason never reached the conversation

adaptive.reason: Antigravity attaches no `trigger: glob` rule since 1.4.7 renamed its file tools: 1.4.6 appends the rule to `view_file`'s result, 1.4.8 appends none to `read_file`'s or after `write_file` (google-antigravity/antigravity-cli#1349). The declaration fails the day a glob rule reaches the model again.
adaptive.measurement: the turn settled after the matching write returned, and no request carried the glob rule's body

adaptive.reason: Antigravity attaches no `trigger: glob` rule since 1.4.7 renamed its file tools: 1.4.6 appends the rule to `view_file`'s result, 1.4.8 appends none to `read_file`'s or after `write_file` (google-antigravity/antigravity-cli#1349). The declaration fails the day a glob rule reaches the model again.
adaptive.measurement: no glob rule reached the model at all, so its early arrival is unobservable while the rule is missing

adaptive.measurement: the plugin's glob rule is copied into the declaring checkout, and no request after the matching write carried it

adaptive.reason: Antigravity's `run_command` declares no working directory: every command runs in the workspace, and a call naming one is refused before any hook runs
adaptive.measurement: the shell calls naming a directory (`Cwd`) reached no hook and left no trace of having run

adaptive.reason: Claude Code reports a post-tool hook's directory after the command ran, so a `cd` inside the command moves it
adaptive.measurement: after `cd <dir>` the post-tool HOOK_WORKDIR named the directory the shell was left in, not the one the command started in
